correctness.rationale: The algebraic threshold is correct. For the generalized amplitude-damping channel with thermal parameter \(n\), the singlet partial-transpose boundary reduces to \(2(1+\sqrt2)n(1-n)\gamma^2+\gamma-1=0\). Independently comparing the positive root with the finite-temperature damping variable in Filippov--Frizen--Kolobova gives exactly their published entanglement-annihilation boundary after identifying \(\gamma=1-e^{-2\Gamma t}\) and \(n(1-n)=w(1-w)\). The diagonal-filter reduction to a unital channel is also consistent with the explicit nonunital-to-unital decomposition in that paper. Thus the final equivalence is mathematically valid, but it is not new.

originality.rationale: A decisive prior source already gives the same exact entanglement-annihilation boundary for two identical finite-temperature generalized amplitude-damping channels. Filippov--Frizen--Kolobova derive the corresponding unital reduction and state in their Eq. (49) that the tensor-square channel is entanglement annihilating exactly beyond the displayed finite-temperature threshold. After the elementary substitution \(\gamma=1-e^{-2\Gamma t}\), their inequality is precisely the quadratic boundary in the audited claim. The later singlet statement adds only the direct PPT calculation showing that one Bell state meets that already-published boundary. The 2025 paper's numerical conjecture therefore does not restore priority over the 2018 exact theorem.
